tagline: Curious about data. Building with code.
about_p1: I’m Douniya, a junior AI and data engineer learning to turn messy data into clear, useful tools. I care about readable code, thoughtful systems, and making technical work feel a bit more human.
about_p2: Right now, I’m exploring Python, notebooks, and how to explain complex ideas simply.

personal_text: Reading about explainability, sketching notebook ideas, and trying to make my next project a little more useful.
contact_text: Feel free to reach out if you’re looking for an AI & Data Engineer, have a question, or just want to connect.
project_avatar_summary: A connected bracelet, an AI model and a mobile app that watch three vital signs, classify asthma risk into three levels and alert loved ones when it turns critical.
project_avatar_results: A complete pipeline working end to end: from a simulated ESP32 sensor to Supabase, a Fuzzy C-Means risk prediction served by FastAPI, and alerts in Flutter.
project_avatar_label: Technology at the service of humanity
project_avatar_tagline: Smart bracelet for asthma attack monitoring
case_invite_text: Looking for a junior AI & Data Engineer, have a question, or just want to connect? Let’s talk.
work_coming_soon_text: This project is still in the making. Its full story will be shared here soon.
project_ats_label: A fair chance for every CV
project_ats_tagline: Explainable CV analysis and candidate matching
project_ats_summary: An intelligent ATS, built during my project at SEWS Kénitra, that reads CVs by meaning rather than keywords and scores candidates on four explainable criteria.
project_ats_results: A modular backend that extracts, structures, validates and scores CVs, with weighted matching (skills 50%, experience 25%, education 15%, languages 10%) that recruiters can inspect.
project_road_tagline: Predicting the severity of road accidents
project_road_summary: My first solo AI project: a classifier trained on more than 4 million real accident records to flag the rare accidents that turn severe.
project_road_results: From a 99%-accurate model that missed almost every severe accident to one that catches 40% of them (7% precision): a hard-won lesson in choosing the right metric.
